newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-MIGHTY DUCKS DROP WILSON AS COACH.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-MIGHTY DUCKS DROP WILSON AS COACH.

text.p: Ron Wilson, who led the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim to their first-ever playoff berth this season, is out as coach of the National Hockey League team.
Anaheim vice president/general manager Jack Ferreira told a news conference Tuesday that the team has decided not to renew Wilson's contract.
"We made a contract proposal to Ron with a month left in the season and got no response from him," said Ferreira. "In fairness to Ron, I think it gives him an opportunity to get a job in the league."
Wilson has been linked as a possible coaching candidate for the Boston Bruins. There are also head coach vacancies in Montreal, Phoenix and San Jose.
Wilson became one of hockey's hottest coaching commodities after he guided the United States to an improbable victory over Canada in the inaugural World Cup championship at Montreal in September.
He followed up that success by leading the Mighty Ducks to their first-ever playoff berth this season.

Anaheim finished with a franchise-best 36-33-13 record and beat Phoenix by four games to three in the first round of the NHL playoffs before falling to Detroit in a four-game sweep in the West semifinals.
The 41-year-old Wilson had a 120-145-31 record in four seasons as coach of the Mighty Ducks.
